entries.title: Proverbs 17:1
segments:
Sacrifices; sumptuous fare from the flesh of slain beasts. 
 
Domestic comfort depends not on outward abundance, but on inward harmony and love.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:2
segments:
Shall have part of the inheritance; his master will give him a share with his own sons. 
 
Wisdom is better than high birth to give influence and honor.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:4
segments: Wicked and corrupt men choose the wicked and corrupt for their companions and accomplices.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:6
segments: It is the ordinance of God that in well-trained families the parents and children shall be a mutual comfort and honor to each other.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:7
segments: Excellent speech; such speech as belongs to men in eminent stations.  He is not fit for a high place, and connot adapt his language to it.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:8
segments:
A gift; given to secure influence. 
 
  Him that hath it; its receiver. 
 
  Whithersoever it turneth it prospereth; as a precious stone reflects its lustre in every way, so a gift is successful in influencing men, whithersoever it is directed.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:9
segments:
Covereth a transgression--repeateth a matter; he who covers a transgression which he has witnessed in another, seeks the peace and harmony of the community, but he who repeats an ill report separates friends. 
 
Peace and harmony can be maintained only by mutual kindness and forbearance; a tale-bearer may embroil a whole community in strife.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:10
segments: Since fools can never learn from experience, their life must be one of perpetual disappointment and trouble, and their end destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:11
segments:
Rebellion; contumacy and sedition towards the magistrate. 
 
  A cruel messenger; a messenger sent by the ruling power to execute vengeance upon him.
The proverb finds its most awful fulfilment in the case of those who rebel against God's righteous government.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:12
segments:
Fool in his folly; that is, a fool acting out his folly in a paroxysm of rage. 
 
Nothing is so unreasonable as folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:14
segments: It is easier to maintain peace in a family or community, that to restore it.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:15
segments: Rulers and judges act in God's behalf, and for the perversion of justice he will call them to an account.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:16
segments:
A price; an opportunity afforded by God. 
 
Since men remain ignorant of God and his salvation, not from the want of opportunities to learn, but becuase they have no heart for it, the justice of God in their destruction will be made manifest to all at the last great day.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:17
segments: Loveth at all times; in adversity, as well as prosperity; the character of a true friend.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:19
segments: Exalteth his gate; the gate to his mansion: a lofty gate implies a sumptuous edifice, the product of ambition and vain-glory.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:22
segments:
A merry heart; a cheerful heart, full of peace and joy. 
 
"A merry heart" is alike honorable to God, in whose righteous government we have always abundant reason to rejoice, and profitable to ourselves; it strengthens the body, and invigorates the powers of the soul.  By indulging ourselves in despondency and discontent we reproach our Maker, impair our physical health, and wither up the noblest faculties of the soul.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:23
segments: A wicked man; privily receives a bribe from the bosom of him whose cause is pending.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:24
segments:
Before him that hath understanding; so that he readily discerns it. 
 
  In the ends of the earth; pursuing folly, so that he never sees true wisdom.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:26
segments: For equity; because of their equity.

entries.title: Proverbs 17:27
segments: A great part of wisdom lies in forbearing to speak, except when we have something important to say.
